title: Event-stream tests depend on fixed sleeps instead of deterministic synchronization
reasoning: The stream-consumer assertions rely on a 100 ms scheduling window for multiple async hops. That can produce false failures on a loaded CI machine or under a slower sanitizer run, even when the production behavior is correct. The same file already uses continuations for sign-in synchronization, so the event path has a weaker synchronization contract than the rest of the suite.
reproduction: Run the affected tests repeatedly under high CPU load or with an injected delay in the stub status/profileStatus calls longer than 100 ms; the assertions can observe stale model state before the consumer task finishes.
recommendation: Replace the sleeps with deterministic test hooks: have the stub expose continuations/counters resumed from status(forSession:) and status(forProfile:), or add a bounded awaitEventually helper that polls the exact model state until it changes or times out with diagnostics.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: These are the tests for the event consumer, but they assert after elapsed wall-clock time rather than after observing that the event was processed.
suggestedRegressionTest: Update at least one stream event test to inject a status call delay greater than 100 ms and prove the new synchronization waits for completion without flaking.
minimumFixScope: CredentialsModelTests event-stream synchronization helper and the tests that currently call Task.sleep.
